text:
Maya: sharing a compact mock for the sidebar regroup — goal is faster scent when people land via links, and fewer clicks to Models/Monitoring. quick reactions?

Tom: looks promising. three buckets (Org / Models / Ops) feel sensible. worried about inconsistent noun vs verb labels though.

Alex: agree with Tom. breadcrumb convention proposal: Org > Workspace > Project > Page. canonical order helps with external links.

Sam: FYI changing the path structure will break old marketplace and docs links. we should support router-level aliases and avoid hash-based primary routing.

Nina: accessibility checklist: always set aria-current on active item, provide a visually-hidden full-breadcrumb string for screen readers, and ensure skip-to-content lands after deep-link navigation.

Jules: mobile UX: collapse to a single label with a chevron that opens an overlay listing each level. tapping a level should navigate and close overlay. overlay must be keyboard accessible.

Maya: mock shows suggested routes: 
/workspaces/:wid/projects/:pid/models/:modelId
/orgs/:oid/workspaces/:wid?panel=metrics#overview
use `panel=` for ephemeral UI state (open panes/modals).

Tom: implementation note: continuous-batching metrics depend on a flat `/models/:id/metrics` endpoint. if we nest models deeper, add an alias to that root path so internal services don't need changes.

Alex: router migration plan: add a redirect/mapping table in the frontend router that 301s old patterns to new canonical routes. keep query params where possible.

Sam: test plan: add e2e that navigates directly to deep link with keyboard only, assert aria-current on sidebar, verify focus is in main content, and ensure overlays/modals open when expected. also emit telemetry event on deep-link landing (route, referrer).

aria-bot: design tickets filed -> https://tickets/redwood/NR-512 (sidebar regroup) and NR-513 (breadcrumbs + routing).

Nina: tiny copy nudge: breadcrumb separator should be `›` (›) for clarity when read aloud. also confirm we expose readable labels (no slugs) in the trail.

Maya: fallback policy proposal: if a deeplink targets an ephemeral modal, route to the parent page and open the modal. do not land users on an orphan modal.

Tom: +1. also recommend we add a small migration banner for users who hit an old permalink during the first A/B week.

Alex: can we A/B the regrouping for 2 weeks on power users? track dropoff and deep-link success rate.

Maya: decision for today: keep canonical resource routes (no hash for primary resources), use `panel=` for ephemeral state, implement router alias map for backwards compat, modal deeplink -> parent page open modal, mobile overlay for collapsed breadcrumbs.

Action items:
- Maya: finalize mocks + copy updates (EOD).
- Sam: implement router alias plan + add E2E tests (tomorrow).
- Tom: scope telemetry and migration banner (this week).
- Nina: compile accessibility checklist + keyboard prototype (next Tue).
- Alex: draft router migration map and redirect rules.
- Jules: mobile overlay prototype and test cases.

Maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll upload the final frames and link them here when ready.

Tom: :eyes: will follow up with a short screen recording of modal fallback flows.
